Begitu banyak hal yang perlu dijelaskan tentang “proses metabolisme”. Berikut ringkasan terstruktur dari konsep dasar hingga jalur utama, pengaturan, dan keterkaitan antar proses.

Apa itu metabolisme dan bagaimana dibagi secara konseptual
- Metabolisme adalah serangkaian reaksi kimia di dalam sel yang mencakup sintesis (anabolisme) dan degradasi (katabolisme) molekul biologis, dengan energi diatur melalui ATP sebagai “uang” energi sel. <cite id="e0c3794b-0">Catabolisme memecah nutrisi untuk menghasilkan energi, sedangkan anabolisme mensintesis molekul kompleks dari bahan sederhana; metabolisme normal mencakup keduanya untuk penggunaan nutrisi dan produksi energi</cite> <cite id="e0c3794b-3">Metabolisme didefinisikan sebagai serangkaian reaksi yang mengarah pada sintesis dan degradasi biomolekul; katabolisme membebaskan energi dengan memecah makromolekul, sementara anabolisme menghabiskan energi untuk biosintesis</cite> <cite id="e0c3794b-4">Energi kimia diukur melalui keseimbangan energi dan ATP sebagai mata uang energi; metabolisme dibagi menjadi katabolisme (pelepasan energi) dan anabolisme (penyerapan energi untuk biosintesis)</cite>.
- Secara spasial, jalur utama terpartisi: glikolisis di sitosol, siklus asam tricarboxilat (TCA) dan fosforilasi oksidatif (mitokondria), dan pada autotrof juga terjadi fiksasi karbon di kloroplas. <cite id="e0c3794b-1">Glikolisis terjadi di sitosol, sedangkan oksidatif fosforilasi di mitokondria</cite> <cite id="e0c3794b-2">Metabolisme mencakup pencernaan bahan, sintesis makromolekul, dan detoksifikasi/eliminasi</cite>.

Bagian katabolik: produksi energi (ATP)
- Glikolisis (sitotol): glukosa → 2 piruvat dengan 2 ATP dan 2 NADH secara bersih; proses anaerobik dan awal dari berbagai “jalur cabang” reduktif (laktat/etanol). <cite id="a0a856cc-0">Satu molekul glukosa diubah menjadi dua molekul piruvat melalui sembilan langkah enzimatik dengan kenaikan bersih 2 ATP dan 2 NADH</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-0">Dalam kondisi aerob, piruvat diangkut ke matriks mitokondria untuk masuk siklus TCA dan OXPHOS</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-4">Glikolisis menghasilkan 2 ATP per glukosa; piruvat juga dapat diubah menjadi asetil-CoA untuk biosintesis</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-1">Dari piruvat, reduktif aliran dapat memulihkan NAD+ melalui dehidrogenase (laktat/etanol) atau memasok ATP melalui fosforilasi oksidatif</cite>.
- Piruvat → asetil-CoA (mitokondria): dekarboksilasi oleh kompleks piruvat dehidrogenase (memerlukan NAD+), menghasilkan asetil-CoA + NADH. <cite id="ddd2d25d-0">Piruvat di dekarboksilasi oleh kompleks piruvat dehidrogenase menjadi asetil-CoA dan NADH di matriks mitokondria</cite>.
- Siklus TCA (mitokondria): asetil-CoA (dari glukosa, asam lemak, atau amino asam) mengkondensasi dengan oksaloasetat membentuk sitrat; setiap putaran menghasilkan 3 NADH, 2 FADH2, dan 1 GTP (≈ATP), serta emisi CO2. <cite id="a0a856cc-0">Setiap asetil-CoA di TCA menghasilkan 3 NADH, 2 FADH2, dan 1 GTP</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Sitrat dihasilkan dari asetil-CoA + oksaloasetat; TCA menghasilkan NADH dan FADH2 yang mentransfer elektron ke rantai respirasi untuk OXPHOS</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-2">TCA juga menyuplai precursor untuk sintesis kolesterol dan asam lemak melalui ACLY yang menghasilkan asetil-CoA nukleus dari sitrat</cite>.
- Rantai transport elektron dan Fosforilasi Oksidatif (OXPHOS): NADH/FADH2 melepas elektron ke kompleks respirasi, menjaga gradien proton dan mendorong ATP sintase menghasilkan ATP; oksigen sebagai akseptor akhir elektron. <cite id="a0a856cc-0">Di OXPHOS, setiap FADH2 menghasilkan 2 ATP dan setiap NADH menghasilkan 3 ATP secara konseptual, dengan konsumsi O2</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Elektron dari NADH/FADH2 menjaga daya tarik proton mitokondria untuk sintesis ATP</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-4">Proses ini menyuplai sebagian besar ATP basal pada sel diferensiasi tinggi, dibandingkan dengan penghasilan ATP yang lebih cepat tapi kurang efisien pada glikolisis</cite>.
- Efisiensi dan fleksibilitas: aerobik menghasilkan sekitar 30–32 ATP/glukosa; hipoksia/keadaan kanker sering beralih ke glikolisis cepat (efek Warburg) meski kurang efisien. <cite id="a0a856cc-0">Dalam kondisi aerob, aliran dari glikolisis→TCA→OXPHOS menghasilkan ~36 ATP per glukosa</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-4">Glikolisis menghasilkan 2 ATP/glukosa dan sering dipakai kanker di hipoksia (efek Warburg)</cite>.

Bagian anabolik: sintesis makromolekul dan precursor
- Jalur biosintesis karbon terintegrasi dengan TCA dan glikolisis: asetil-CoA (dari glukosa/lemak/AA) dan TCA intermediates menyediakan karbon/elektron untuk lemak, nukleotida, protein, dan modifikasi epigenetik. <cite id="ddd2d25d-0">Asetil-CoA dari glukosa dan asam lemak mengalir ke TCA; sitrat juga diangkut ke sitosol untuk diubah kembali menjadi asetil-CoA oleh ATP citrate lyase untuk sintesis lemak; ketersediaan asetil-CoA juga mendukung histon asetilasi</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-2">Intermedi TCA mengarah pada biosintesis lipid, nukleotida, dan protein, serta modifikasi kromatin dan DNA</cite>.
- Jalur karbohidrat anabolik: glikogenogenesis (glukosa→glikogen), dan glukoneogenesis (non-karbohidrat→glukosa: laktat, glicerol, asam amino glukogenik), dengan pengaturan hormon yang berlawanan. <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Glukoneogenesis mensintesis glukosa dari laktat, glicerol, dan asam amino glukogenik untuk menjaga kadar gula darah</cite>.
- Jalur asam amino: transaminasi dan deaminasi menyediakan α-ketoasam untuk glikolisis/TCA/lemak; amonia diubah menjadi urea di hati untuk ekskresi. <cite id="ddd2d25d-1">Asam amino rantai cabang (BCAA) menghasilkan unit karbon yang mengarah ke TCA, ketone body, dan lipogenesis; valin glukogenik (succinil-CoA), leusin ketogenik (asetoasetat, asetil-CoA)</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Asam amino deaminasi menghasilkan amonia yang diubah menjadi urea via siklus ornitin di hati; α-ketoasam memasuki jalur glukosa/lemak</cite>.
- Jalur lemak: lipogenesis mengubah asetil-CoA menjadi asam lemak simpan di adipositas; β-oksidasinya kembali menghasilkan asetil-CoA untuk TCA. <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Asam lemak dihidrolisis menjadi asilkarinit; asil-CoA dioksidasikan menghasilkan asetil-CoA yang masuk TCA untuk energi</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-0">Sitrat dari TCA diubah kembali menjadi asetil-CoA oleh ACL untuk sintesis lemak</cite>.
- Jalur energi alternatif dan penyesuaian redoks: pada iskemia/hipoksia, peningkatan NADH menghambat dehidrogenase, respirasi menurun, dan glikolisis anaerob meningkat dengan produksi laktat; penurunan pasokan oksigen juga membatasi β-oksidsi lemak. <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Peningkatan NADH pada hipoksia menghambat glikeraldehida-3-P dehidrogenase sehingga glikolisis terbatas; O2 yang berkurang menyebabkan penurunan ATP/PCr dan peningkatan glikolisis anaerob serta laktat</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Pada iskemia, kandungan sitosol asetil-CoA dan karnitin berkurang, menunjukkan β-oksidsi terbatas; jantung dapat beralih dari lemak ke glukosa oksidasi</cite>.

Regulasi dan keseimbangan energi
- Pusat regulasi energi: ATP/ADP dan NADH/NAD+ sebagai ko-faktor kunci; ketersediaan oksigen menentukan preferensi glikolisis vs. OXPHOS. <cite id="a0a856cc-0">OXPHOS menghasilkan ATP secara efisien dengan konsumsi oksigen</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Umpan balik dari TCA/respirasi ke piruvat dehidrogenase terutama melalui rasio NADH/NAD+ dan asetil-CoA/CoASH, bukan hanya ATP/ADP</cite>.
- Enzim penghambat dan titik kontrol utama: glikolisis memiliki tiga enzim rate-limiting (glukokinase/HK, PFK, piruvat kinase); piruvat dehidrogenase terregulasi oleh NADH/NAD+, asetil-CoA, dan senyawa terkait. <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Glikolisis memiliki tiga enzim kritis: HK, PFK, dan piruvat kinase; ATP menghambat aktivitas HK dan PFK</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-0">PDH mengubah piruvat menjadi asetil-CoA menghasilkan NADH; aktivitasnya dipengaruhi ketersediaan NAD+ dan aliran TCA/oksigen</cite>.
- Pengaturan hormonal dan sistemik: insulin meningkatkan pengambilan dan penggunaan glukosa, menekan glukoneogenesis, serta meningkatkan sintesis lemak/protein; glukagon dan kortisol meningkatkan glukosa darah, merangsang lipolisis dan glukoneogenesis. <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Insulin mempromosikan penggunaan glukosa dan menghambat glukoneogenesis; glukagon meningkatkan glukosa darah, memicu lipolisis dan glukoneogenesis</cite>.
- Keterkaitan redoks dan epigenetik: kadar asetil-CoA dan NAD(H) memengaruhi asetilasi histon dan kapasitas sintesis, menjembatani metabolisme dan ekspresi gen. <cite id="ddd2d25d-0">Penurunan glukosa dan sintesis lemak di bawah keadaan puasa meningkatkan oksidasi lemak untuk menjaga asetil-CoA untuk ATP dan tubuh keto; ketersediaan asetil-CoA mendukung histon asetilasi</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-2">Intermedi TCA dan asetil-CoA berkontribusi pada modifikasi kromatin dan regulasi gen metabolisme</cite>.

Kompartementalisasi organel dan ruang lingkup spasial
- Mitokondria: “pabrik ATP” dengan matriks TCA dan membran dalam Rantai Transport Elektron/ATP sintase; juga situs β-oksidsi lemak, siklus urea (hepatosel), dan koneksi ke jalur karbohidrat. <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Mitokondria mengoksidasi glukosa, asam amino, dan lemak, menghubungkan TCA dengan OXPHOS; glukosa dan lemak diubah menjadi asetil-CoA</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Asetil-CoA dari lemak dioksidasikan di mitokondria, kemudian masuk TCA; gliserol dari lipolisis dapat memasuki glukoneogenesis</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Ammonia dari deaminasi asam amino diubah menjadi urea melalui siklus ornitin di hati</cite>.
- Sitosol dan ER/Retikulum Endoplasma: glikolisis di sitosol; ER dan lisosom berperan dalam glikogen (penyimpanan dan degradasi fosforilase/transferase), dan sitosol menyediakan nodus kontrol untuk glikoneogenesis (pirogratifikasi piruvat dari glukosa-6-fosfat). <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Glikolisis di sitosol dengan tiga enzim rate-limiting; ATP menghambat HK dan PFK</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Piruvat dari glikolisis dapat diubah menjadi asetil-CoA untuk lemak; glukosa juga dihasilkan dari non-karbohidrat melalui glukoneogenesis</cite>.
- Dalam sel saraf jantung iskemia: terjadi peralihan sumber karbon dan perbaikan distribusi ATP (substrat-level fosforilasi dan peningkatan laktat), menunjukkan fleksibilitas kompartemen metabolisme. <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Pada iskemia, peningkatan glikolisis dan produksi laktat meningkatkan ATP generasi secara anaerob; aliran substrat cepat memungkinkan penyesuaian</cite>.
- Pada autotrof: kloroplas melakukan fiksasi karbon (fotosintesis) yang menghasilkan glukosa, menyediakan reduktor (NADPH) dan prekursor karbon untuk biosintesis; hubungan timbal balik dengan mitokondria. <cite id="e0c3794b-1">Selain glikolisis dan OXPHOS, autotrof juga memiliki kloroplas untuk fiksasi karbon (fotosintesis) yang mensintesis glukosa</cite>.

Contoh keterpaduan end-ke-end dan shuttle elektron/reduktif
- Jalur kardiovaskular iskemia/reaksif: penurunan O2 menyebabkan penurunan ATP/PCr dan peningkatan Pi yang mendorong glikolisis anaerob dan laktat; pada saat yang sama, aliran asil dari lemak terbatas dan jantung beralih ke glukosa; pengaturan redoks NADH/NAD+ mengendalikan PDH dan aliran ke TCA. <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Pada iskemia, penurunan O2 memicu peningkatan glikolisis, laktat, penurunan asetil-CoA dan karnitin; jantung beralih dari β-oksida ke glukosa oksidasi</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Umpan balik redoks NADH/NAD+ dan asetil-CoA/CoASH mengendalikan PDH dan aliran TCA</cite>.
- Jalur shuttle reduktor: perbedaan pengangkutan elektron dari sitosol ke matriks (glikeralddehidase vs. malat shuttle) mengubah efisiensi ATP dari glikolisis; ini menjelaskan variasi yield antar jaringan. <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Perbedaan shuttle (glikeralddehidase vs. malat) mengubah moles ATP per glukosa, karena transfer lambat dan menjadi titik batas antara sitosol dan matriks</cite>.

Pertanyaan umum dan jawaban praktis (yang sering muncul)
- Apa bedanya anabolisme dan katabolisme? <cite id="e0c3794b-0">Katabolisme memecah molekul untuk melepas energi (misalnya glukosa→piruvat→asetil-CoA), sedangkan anabolisme mensintesis molekul kompleks dengan menghabiskan energi (misalnya asetil-CoA→sitrat→jalan biosintesis)</cite> <cite id="e0c3794b-3">Katabolisme membebaskan energi (CO2, air, amonia), anabolisme menghabiskan energi untuk biomolekul</cite>.
- Mengapa OXPHOS efisien tapi butuh oksigen? <cite id="a0a856cc-0">OXPHOS mentransfer elektron dari NADH/FADH2 melalui kompleks respirasi ke O2; setiap NADH/FADH2 menghasilkan 2–3 ATP dan O2 sebagai akseptor akhir, sehingga efisien tetapi oksigen mutlak</cite>.
- Titik kontrol utama glikolisis? <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Hexokinase, PFK, dan piruvat kinase; ATP dan NADH menghambat HK dan PFK</cite>.
- Bagaimana asam amino terlibat dalam energi? <cite id="ddd2d25d-1">BCAA dioksidasi/transformasi menghasilkan asetoasetat dan asetil-CoA (ketogenik) atau succinil-CoA (glukogenik), menjembatani TCA, ketone bodies, dan lipogenesis</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Deaminasi asam amino menghasilkan amonia (urea) dan α-ketoasam yang masuk glukoneogenesis/β-oksidsi</cite>.
- Bagaimana keseimbangan energi diatur? <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Insulin vs. glukagon/kortikosteroid mengarahkan antara penyerapan dan pelepasan glukosa, lipolisis vs. lipogenesis, serta sintesis vs. catabolisme protein</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Rasio NADH/NAD+ dan asetil-CoA/CoASH mengatur PDH dan flux TCA secara hormonal-like</cite>.

Penutup: gambaran makro dan mikro
- Secara makroskopis, metabolisme adalah keseimbangan dinamis antara “menguras” energi (katabolisme) dan “mengisi” materi (anabolisme) untuk menjaga homeostasis dan pertumbuhan, dengan ATP sebagai mata uang pengukur. <cite id="e0c3794b-1">Katabolisme dan anabolisme saling terkait, dengan glikolisis di sitosol dan OXPHOS di mitokondria sebagai poros energi</cite> <cite id="e0c3794b-4">Energi intake, storage, dan expenditure dipertahankan melalui regulasi ATP</cite>.
- Secara mikroskopis, proses ini terkoordinasi antar enzim, organel, dan jalur: glukosa di sitosol menjadi piruvat, asetil-CoA di mitokondria mengalir ke TCA dan OXPHOS untuk ATP, sedangkan reduktor dan intermedi juga memelihara biosintesis lemak, nukleotida, dan protein; pada saat darurat, sel mampu beralih antara sumber karbon dan menyesuaikan laju produksi ATP. <cite id="a0a856cc-0">Glikolisis→TCA→OXPHOS adalah poros energi dengan yield tinggi di bawah aerob</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-2">Mitokondria menghubungkan oksidasi substrat dengan sintesis ATP dan menyediakan precursor untuk sintesis lipid</cite> <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Gula, lemak, dan asam amino saling melengkapi melalui piruvat, asetil-CoA, dan α-ketoasam, dengan pengaturan hormonal yang ketat</cite>.

Catatan lanjutan
- Untuk autotrof (tumbuhan, alga, bakteri fiksator karbon): tambahkan penjelasan siklus Calvin di kloroplas (fiksasi CO2→ribulosa bisfosfat→fosfoenolpiruvat→karboksilasi→regenerasi/produksi glukosa) yang menyediakan glukosa dan NADPH untuk biosintesis dan respirasi. <cite id="e0c3794b-1">Kloroplas memainkan peran kunci di autotrof untuk fiksasi karbon</cite>.
- Untuk sensor sinyal energi intraseluler, penekanan pada AMPK (aktif saat ATP rendah/AMP tinggi) dan mTORC1 (aktif saat energi/AA cukup) akan melengkapi bagian regulasi, termasuk keterkaitan dengan mitokondria dan jalur glikogen/lemak. <cite id="ddd2d25d-4">Kontrol allosterik dan hormonal diimbangi perubahan ekspresi gen untuk menjaga keseimbangan energi</cite> <cite id="a0a856cc-3">Perubahan redoks dan ketersediaan substrat memicu adaptasi mitokondria dan flux metabolik</cite>.

Title: Metformin and glioma: Targeting metabolic dysregulation for enhanced therapeutic outcomes
Snippet: In normal cells, metabolism of glucose and production of ATP is conducted in three main stages of glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). During glycolysis, one molecule of glucose is converted to two molecules of pyruvate over nine enzyme-catalyzed steps with a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH molecules. Each pyruvate is then converted to acetyl-CoA which enters the TCA cycle during which 3 NADH, 2 FADH2 and one GTP molecules are produced. Finally, in OXPHOS, each FADH2 and NADH molecule is converted to two and three ATP molecules respectively with a concomitant consumption of molecular oxygen, making this stage the major source of ATP production in normal cells. Snippet: The Tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle (citric acid cycle or Krebs cycle) comprises a series of reactions occurring in the mitochondrial matrix, involving numerous substrates crucial to cellular metabolism (Figure 1). Metabolites of the TCA cycle regulate cellular function. They are necessary for the biosynthesis of lipids, nucleotides, and proteins (McDonnell et al., 2016), as well as chromatin modifications, DNA methylation, and posttranslational protein modifications (Wellen et al., 2009;Moussaieff et al., 2015). The TCA cycle is initiated by a reaction that produces six-carbon citrate from two-carbon acetyl-CoA. Acetyl-CoA is generated from the oxidation of amino acids, glucose, fatty acids, or pyruvate (Figure 2). Acetyl-CoA combines with a four-carbon oxaloacetate molecule to yield citrate, which initiates the TCA cycle (Figure 2). Then, the oxidative decarboxylation of citrate isomer, isocitrate, forms αketoglutarate, a five-carbon molecule. Conversion of αketoglutarate to succinyl-CoA, a four-carbon molecule, yields two carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and two nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH or NAD + ) molecules. Succinyl-CoA is then converted into succinate-producing GTP, which can later be converted into ATP (Shi and Tu, 2015;Martínez-Reyes et al., 2016). Oxidation of succinate to four-carbon fumarate transfers two hydrogens to flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), forming FADH 2 (hydroquinone form). Lastly, fumarate is converted to malate and oxaloacetate, forming acetyl-CoA to proceed with the cycle (Martínez-Reyes and Chandel, 2020) (Figure 2). As detailed in the next section, byproducts NADH and FADH 2 from the TCA cycle are essential electron donors for mitochondrial OXPHOS (Figure 2).

Title: Metformin and glioma: Targeting metabolic dysregulation for enhanced therapeutic outcomes
Snippet: In normal cells, metabolism of glucose and production of ATP is conducted in three main stages of glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). During glycolysis, one molecule of glucose is converted to two molecules of pyruvate over nine enzyme-catalyzed steps with a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH molecules. Each pyruvate is then converted to acetyl-CoA which enters the TCA cycle during which 3 NADH, 2 FADH2 and one GTP molecules are produced. Finally, in OXPHOS, each FADH2 and NADH molecule is converted to two and three ATP molecules respectively with a concomitant consumption of molecular oxygen, making this stage the major source of ATP production in normal cells. In cancer cells, including glioma cells, metabolic reprogramming promotes glycolysis as the main provider of ATP, whilst concurrently stalling TCA cycle and OXPHOS. Whilst this makes the yield of ATP per molecule of glucose less efficient, this is compensated for by faster production of ATP. Mechanisms for this reprogramming are discussed below.

In addition, pyruvate enters the TCA cycle via acetyl-CoA to produce 1 mol ATP and 3 mol NADH under aerobic conditions. Snippet: To face anabolic demands and supply the required energy for homeostasis, cells undergo metabolic reprogramming. Mitochondria play an essential role in this process, by oxidizing glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids and by linking the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle to oxidative phosphorylation (Figure 2). 

The TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation are highly efficient to generate ATP. Pyruvate or fatty acids transferred to the mitochondrial matrix are oxidized into acetyl CoA to enter the TCA cycle through condensation with oxaloacetate to form citrate. Citrate can be exported to the cytosol following oxidation by the TCA cycle or following hydrolysis by ATP citrate lyase (ACLY) to regenerate oxaloacetate and acetyl CoA, needed to synthetize cholesterol and fatty acids. The TCA cycle produces NADH and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FADH2), which provide electrons to the electron transport chain to support oxidative phosphorylation and generate about 30-32 ATP molecules from 1 molecule of glucose converted into pyruvate (Figure 2). Glutamate can also fuel the TCA cycle through its conversion into αketoglutarate by glutaminolysis. In contrast to oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis produces ATP from glucose rapidly but very inefficiently (2 ATP/molecule of glucose). Glycolysis involves 3 rate-limiting enzymes, including hexokinases (HKs), PFK, and the pyruvate kinases. The first step of glycolysis is the uptake of glucose by the cell and its transformation by HK1 into glucose-6-phosphate that can enter the pentose phosphate pathway, providing nucleotides and amino acids precursors.

TCA cycle must be under a strict control to both respond to energetic demands and to prevent major disturbances. Conceptually, such kind of regulation must be hormonal-like. Imbalances leading to sustained accumulation of TCA cycle intermediates may lead to aberrant sequestering of carbons. TCA cycle must be under a strict control to both respond to energetic demands and to prevent major disturbances. Conceptually, such kind of regulation must be hormonal-like. We here present all the possibilities that directly and indirectly would allow fast and strong regulation of the TCA cycle flux and the TCA cycle metabolite concentrations. The tight regulation of PyrDH makes possible to accelerate or decelerate acetyl-CoA production. The increase in acetyl-CoA leads to increase the flux through the cycle and the production of NADH/FADH 2 ; and the opposite if the production of acetyl-CoA is decreased. However, availability of acetyl-CoA would not restore steady state in a fully unbalanced TCA cycle. Neither, major alterations in PyrDH activity would lead to a TCA cycle imbalance. 

Hormonal-like control of enzymes related to anaplerotic reactions Oxalacetate entrance to TCA cycle may occur via pyruvate carboxylase (requires ATP). As far as we know, regulation by phosphorylation/dephosphorylation has not been reported, but allosterically by acetyl-CoA and aspartate [76] . From our point of view, the enzyme is expected to be regulated by post-translational modifications driven by hormonal-like mechanisms. In 2010 J.C. Wallace wrote: "with only a little over 2,000 papers listed by PubMed in response to a search for "pyruvate carboxylase," it is not surprising that there remain many questions to be answered about this complex enzyme and its diverse functions" [77] . In 2022 we still lack relevant information on the regulation of this enzyme. 

The entrance via α-ketoglutarate must be tightly controlled to keep a balanced Krebs cycle. This is unlikely to occur via the reaction involved in such event: glutamate transaminase (also known as aspartate/glutamate transaminase).

documents.snippet: In normal cells, metabolism of glucose and production of ATP is conducted in three main stages of glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). During glycolysis, one molecule of glucose is converted to two molecules of pyruvate over nine enzyme-catalyzed steps with a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH molecules. Each pyruvate is then converted to acetyl-CoA which enters the TCA cycle during which 3 NADH, 2 FADH2 and one GTP molecules are produced. Finally, in OXPHOS, each FADH2 and NADH molecule is converted to two and three ATP molecules respectively with a concomitant consumption of molecular oxygen, making this stage the major source of ATP production in normal cells. In cancer cells, including glioma cells, metabolic reprogramming promotes glycolysis as the main provider of ATP, whilst concurrently stalling TCA cycle and OXPHOS. Whilst this makes the yield of ATP per molecule of glucose less efficient, this is compensated for by faster production of ATP. Mechanisms for this reprogramming are discussed below.

Succinyl-CoA is then converted into succinate-producing GTP, which can later be converted into ATP (Shi and Tu, 2015;Martínez-Reyes et al., 2016). documents.snippet: The Tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle (citric acid cycle or Krebs cycle) comprises a series of reactions occurring in the mitochondrial matrix, involving numerous substrates crucial to cellular metabolism (Figure 1). Metabolites of the TCA cycle regulate cellular function. They are necessary for the biosynthesis of lipids, nucleotides, and proteins (McDonnell et al., 2016), as well as chromatin modifications, DNA methylation, and posttranslational protein modifications (Wellen et al., 2009;Moussaieff et al., 2015). The TCA cycle is initiated by a reaction that produces six-carbon citrate from two-carbon acetyl-CoA. Acetyl-CoA is generated from the oxidation of amino acids, glucose, fatty acids, or pyruvate (Figure 2). Acetyl-CoA combines with a four-carbon oxaloacetate molecule to yield citrate, which initiates the TCA cycle (Figure 2). Then, the oxidative decarboxylation of citrate isomer, isocitrate, forms αketoglutarate, a five-carbon molecule. Conversion of αketoglutarate to succinyl-CoA, a four-carbon molecule, yields two carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and two nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH or NAD + ) molecules. Succinyl-CoA is then converted into succinate-producing GTP, which can later be converted into ATP (Shi and Tu, 2015;Martínez-Reyes et al., 2016). Oxidation of succinate to four-carbon fumarate transfers two hydrogens to flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), forming FADH 2 (hydroquinone form). Lastly, fumarate is converted to malate and oxaloacetate, forming acetyl-CoA to proceed with the cycle (Martínez-Reyes and Chandel, 2020) (Figure 2). As detailed in the next section, byproducts NADH and FADH 2 from the TCA cycle are essential electron donors for mitochondrial OXPHOS (Figure 2).

Title: The Warburg Effect: Is it Always an Enemy?
Snippet: In the past, it was assumed that the Warburg effect refers to the preference of cancer cells to produce energy via glycolysis even in the presence of sufficient oxygen, which differs from the traditional 'anaerobic' glycolysis seen in cells without mitochondria [20]. Moreover, erythrocytes lack mitochondria, but they have abundant oxygen. Thus, another question to be answered is whether erythrocytes utilize the 'anaerobic' or 'aerobic' glycolysis for ATP regeneration. 

Inspired by my student's questions and the insightful opinion paper by Schurr [16], this review explores the significance of the Warburg effect, examining how tumor cells adapt to their microenvironment and respond to oncogenic and tumor suppressor gene signaling. Moreover, this review highlights that the Warburg effect is not a privilege of cancer cells only and that normal cells may produce ATP mainly via glycolysis, despite having active mitochondria and abundant oxygen, a process similar to the Warburg effect. This review also contends that glycolysis is a singular pathway, with the key difference lying in the fate of pyruvate, which is considered the 'end product' of glycolysis. The fate of pyruvate determines the extent to which normal and cancer cells utilize the Warburg effect [22]. Finally, it discusses recent advancements in targeted therapies based on metabolic alterations observed in the Warburg effect. To avoid any further confusion in this review, 'aerobic glycolysis' will be referred to as the Warburg effect or Warburg-like glycolysis.

In the past, it was assumed that the Warburg effect refers to the preference of cancer cells to produce energy via glycolysis even in the presence of sufficient oxygen, which differs from the traditional 'anaerobic' glycolysis seen in cells without mitochondria [20]. However, some cells, such as retina and immune cells, produce ATP using a process that resembles the Warburg effect; i.e., they convert pyruvate to lactate despite having fully active mitochondria and a sufficient amount of oxygen [21]. Moreover, erythrocytes lack mitochondria, but they have abundant oxygen. Thus, another question to be answered is whether erythrocytes utilize the 'anaerobic' or 'aerobic' glycolysis for ATP regeneration. 

Inspired by my student's questions and the insightful opinion paper by Schurr [16], this review explores the significance of the Warburg effect, examining how tumor cells adapt to their microenvironment and respond to oncogenic and tumor suppressor gene signaling. Moreover, this review highlights that the Warburg effect is not a privilege of cancer cells only and that normal cells may produce ATP mainly via glycolysis, despite having active mitochondria and abundant oxygen, a process similar to the Warburg effect. This review also contends that glycolysis is a singular pathway, with the key difference lying in the fate of pyruvate, which is considered the 'end product' of glycolysis. The fate of pyruvate determines the extent to which normal and cancer cells utilize the Warburg effect [22]. Finally, it discusses recent advancements in targeted therapies based on metabolic alterations observed in the Warburg effect. To avoid any further confusion in this review, 'aerobic glycolysis' will be referred to as the Warburg effect or Warburg-like glycolysis.

These are the malate/oxaloacetate (MAL/OAA), the malate/aspartate (MAL/ASP), the glycerolphosphate/dihydroxyacetone-phosphate (G3P/DHAP), the proline/glutamate (PRO/GLU) and the L-lactate/pyruvate (L-LAC/PYR).

This shuttle also requires two transporters, the a-KG/malate antiporter (encoded by SLC25A11 gene), which transfers cytosolic malate into the mitochondrial matrix; and the aspartate/glutamate antiporter (encoded by SLC25A13 gene), which transfers mitochondrial aspartate into the cytosol (106). Cytosolic GPDH oxidizes NADH to NAD + in conjunction with the reduction of dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) to glycerol-3phosphate, whereas mitochondrial GPDH catalyzes the reverse reaction that oxidizes glycerol-3-phosphate into DHAP and reduces FAD into FADH 2 . Therefore, such shuttle mechanisms enable cells to maintain adequate NAD + in the cytosol in support of glycolysis and sufficient NADH in the mitochondria in support of OXPHOS. 

Like NADH, NADP(H) cannot diffuse across the mitochondrial inner membrane (10,76,112). The exchange of cytosolic and mitochondrial NADP(H) pools is, therefore, carried out by the isocitrate-a-KG shuttle through IDH1 and IDH2 isozymes (35,73,106) (Fig. 4). Cytosolic IDH1 and mitochondrial IDH2 catalyze the reversible interconversion between isocitrate and a-KG in conjunction with the interconversion of NADP + and NADPH (106). This shuttle also requires two carrier proteins, the citrate carrier protein (encoded by SLC25A1 gene), which exports mitochondrial isocitrate into the cytosol in exchange for malate; and the a-KG/ malate antiporter, which is the same carrier as in the malate/ aspartate shuttle (106). The malate-aspartate shuttle (Fig. 1) plays a major role in the movement of reducing equivalents (NADH) into, or out of, the mitochondrion. This is particularly important when the rate of glycolysis is high; production of NADH from glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase activity decreases the cytosolic NAD + /NADH ratio. This NADH imbalance can be partially restored by other dehydrogenases such as lactate dehydrogenase and cytosolic glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (cGPD), but is mainly driven by the phosphorylation state of the cytosolic adenine nucleotide system (i.e. [ATP]/[ADP].[Pi] [56]). In the brain, as in the liver, the phosphorylation status determines the redox status, with the components of the aspartate aminotransferase maintaining equilibrium across a broad range of glycolytic activity [57]. Cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase (GOT1) converts cytosolic aspartate to oxaloacetate which can then be converted by cytosolic malate dehydrogenase to malate, regenerating cytosolic NAD + . The malate is then transported into the mitochondrion and reconverted to oxaloacetate by mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase, generating NADH within the mitochondrion; thus successfully transporting a proton from cytosol to the mitochondrial matrix, supporting oxidative phosphorylation. 

Glycolysis is not the only generator of cytosolic NADH. The NAD + -linked phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase also generates cytosolic NADH when oxidising 3-phosphoglycerate, a key step in the serine and glycine biosynthesis pathway (Fig. 1). Defects in the malate-aspartate shuttle have been shown to disrupt NADH homeostasis in HEK293 cells, leading to lack of serine and impairments in one-carbon metabolism [58].

Title: Exploring the proton transport mechanism of the mitochondrial ADP/ATP carrier: FA‐cycling hypothesis and beyond
